questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. After the gate is raised, wait until you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no trains are coming before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: When do large trucks lose speed?

options.text: Driving up long or steep hills.
Driving in long, gradual curves.
Driving down long, gradual hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take longer to speed up than smaller vehicles. They lose speed when driving up long or steep hills. Leave extra space between you and a large truck, especially on hills.

questions.question: When is it safe to move back into the right lane after passing another vehicle on the left?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can move back into the right lane when you can see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, take your foot off the accelerator to slow down gradually. Do not use the brakes until the vehicle has slowed down significantly.

questions.question: When are streets and highways most slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after it starts to rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery during the first 30 minutes of rain. Water mixes with oil and chemicals on the road that have not washed away yet, creating a slippery surface. Drive carefully when it first starts to rain.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When you cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your original lane, make sure you are not too close to the vehicle you passed. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to return safely.

questions.question: What lane must you be in to make a left turn from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning, use the lane closest to the direction you want to turn into. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead has many curves.
There is a sharp curve in the road ahead.
The road ahead may be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead may be slippery.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What problems can sudden wind gusts on highways cause?

options.text: They generally affect only large vehicles.
They only cause visibility problems.
They can affect all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can affect all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind can cause problems for all drivers, not just large vehicles. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dirt and dust, and it can also physically push a vehicle sideways.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn drivers about hazards ahead. Round signs are used only to warn about railroad crossings.

questions.question: How should drivers check their blind spots when changing lanes?

options.text: Only use the left outside mirror.
Look over your left or right shoulder.
Only use the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas around your car that mirrors cannot show. Look over the correct shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: By looking in your side mirrors.
By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
By looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas your mirrors cannot show. Turn your head and look over your shoulders to check these areas.

questions.question: What happens when you slow down to look at accidents or unusual things on the road?

options.text: It causes traffic jams.
It prevents rear-end collisions.
It improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It causes traffic jams.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at accidents or unusual things. This slowing down, called rubbernecking, creates traffic jams.

questions.question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line, it is safe to drive.
If you are below the legal alcohol limit, you can drive safely.
Alcohol affects your judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects your judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms your judgment. You need good judgment to drive safely. Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your driving ability, even if you are below the legal limit.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: The same as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: When merging onto a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: Find a gap large enough for you to safely enter the traffic flow. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there are no safe gaps to merge into.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your headlights on low beam.
Use high beams until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
Use high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlights on low beam.
questions.explanation: Use high beams only in rural areas when other cars are far away. Switch to low beams when you are following another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop at the crosswalk.
Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guard signals you to go.
Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: This five-sided sign means you are near a school. Watch carefully and stop if children are crossing.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing red light?

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Stop completely, check traffic, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check traffic, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: How do you see vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulders to check these areas.

questions.question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Wait for the green light before going.
Slow down and cross carefully.
Stop before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution. Watch for other traffic and pedestrians before crossing.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
They all have air brakes that stop quickly.
They are easier to steer than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need much more distance to stop. At 55 mph, a passenger vehicle stops in about 400 feet. A large truck at the same speed needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: Which statement about medications and driving is true?

options.text: Most cold medications can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medications are safe if you follow the recommended dose.
Prescribed medications are always safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medications, prescription or over-the-counter, can affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy. You must know how your medication affects your ability to drive.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly without warning.
Check for other vehicles in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly without warning.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes. Use your turn signal to warn other drivers. Make sure no vehicles are in the space you want to enter.
